To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fermionic determinant for an SU(N) calaron with nontrivial monopole holonomy is given by the product of the fermionic determinants for each monopole, with the latter being the product of a constant and the exponential of a linear function in the monopole separation.

the fermionic determinant of an SU(N) calaron with nontrivial asymptotic holonomy has the form of a sum over N monopoles and that it has a leading term of order N and an order N^2 correction, both of which can be computed analytically.

(i) the functional determinant of the caloron is exponentially suppressed as a power of the separation between dyons; (ii) this power is equal to the number of dyons minus 1, which is the difference between the number of monopoles and the number of antimonopoles; (iii) the power is independent of the holonomy at the spatial infinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics.
the study of the functional determinant for SU(2) and SU(3) fermionic fields in the background of instantons with nontrivial spatial asymptotics.
the study of nonperturbative phenomena in the Yang-Mills theory, in particular with the fermionic zero modes in the background of instantons with nontrivial asymptotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fermionic determinant in the fundamental representation is not a simple product of N fermionic determinants for each dyon.
the fermionic determinant in the presence of the caloron background is a function of N and is given by the product of the fermionic determinants in the presence of N monopoles.
the instanton-dyon picture of the caloron with non-trivial holonomy is not a viable alternative to the instanton-dyons picture in the large-N limit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at large separations, the fermion zero modes of the caloron are localized at the positions of the dyons.

the fermionic determinant is a product of the determinants of the monopoles and the instanton, and the latter is the same as the determinant for an instanton in a flat space, which has been known for a long time.

the fermionic determinant for a caloron with nonvanishing holonomy is given by the product of the determinants of N fermions in the background of a single dyon and the determinant of a fermion in the adjoint representation in the background of N dyons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fermionic determinant is exponentially suppressed at large separations.
the fermionic determinant is not a smooth function of the separation between dyons.
the fermionic determinant is nonanalytic in the separation between dyons and the nonanalyticity is of a nonperturbative nature.
